title: Balancing Producer Fairness and Efficiency via Prior-Weighted Rating System Design
source_inventory_policy: Independent source-first inventory from the pinned ICWSM PDF. Local source.txt line ranges are OCR navigation aids; paper page, section, theorem, and equation locators are authoritative. The inventory includes all mathematical formulas, metrics, named results, and the responsive-market choice rule; raw datasets, calibrated estimates, plots, and simulator implementation are empirical non-theorem scope. Lean identifiers are routing only, never semantic evidence.

mbjg25_eq1_posterior_rating.statement: Equation 1 defines the posterior mean rating after binary feedback as (alpha_hat + R(v,t)) / (alpha_hat + beta_hat + |S(v,t)|).

mbjg25_fixed_posterior_mean.statement: After fixing prior shape (alpha_tilde,beta_tilde) and strength eta, the conditional expected posterior rating in the fixed model is (eta*alpha_tilde + t*q_v) / (eta*alpha_tilde + eta*beta_tilde + t).
mbjg25_fixed_posterior_mean.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), pp. 1013-1015, Sections 2.1 and Appendix A derivation; source.txt:203-276 and 1497-1517

mbjg25_fixed_bias.statement: The fixed-model bias is the conditional expected posterior rating minus true product quality q_v.
mbjg25_fixed_bias.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1014, Equation 3 and Appendix A; source.txt:333-341 and 1497-1517

mbjg25_fixed_variance.statement: The fixed-model conditional variance of the posterior rating is t*q_v*(1-q_v)/(eta*alpha_tilde + eta*beta_tilde + t)^2.

mbjg25_fixed_squared_bias.statement: The squared-bias component is the square of conditional expected posterior rating minus true quality.
mbjg25_fixed_squared_bias.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1014, Equation 3 and Appendix A; source.txt:333-341 and 1497-1517

mbjg25_eq2_fixed_market_mse.statement: Equation 2 defines fixed-market MSE as the average over products of squared posterior-rating error relative to true quality.

mbjg25_eq3_fixed_bias_variance_decomposi.statement: Equation 3 states that conditional mean squared error for one product equals squared conditional bias plus conditional variance.

mbjg25_theorem3_1_variance_closed_interv.statement: Corrected Theorem 3.1 variance conclusion: on 0 <= q_v <= 1, increasing nonnegative prior strength weakly decreases posterior-rating variance.
mbjg25_theorem3_1_variance_closed_interv.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1015, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A Equations 11 and 14-15; source.txt:443-450 and 1533-1552 and 1638-1650
mbjg25_theorem3_1_variance_closed_interv.source_note: The printed theorem says strictly decreasing on the closed Bernoulli interval. The corrected weak endpoint is paired with a strict interior theorem and checked endpoint counterexamples.

mbjg25_theorem3_1_variance_strict_interi.statement: Corrected Theorem 3.1 strict conclusion: for 0 < q_v < 1, positive elapsed reviews, positive prior-shape mass, and a strict increase in nonnegative prior strength, posterior-rating variance strictly decreases.
mbjg25_theorem3_1_variance_strict_interi.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1015, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A Equations 11 and 14-15; source.txt:443-450 and 1533-1552 and 1638-1650
mbjg25_theorem3_1_variance_strict_interi.source_note: This repairs the printed statement's endpoint-domain slip without changing its substantive interior monotonicity conclusion.

mbjg25_theorem3_1_squared_bias_monotonic.statement: Theorem 3.1 states that squared conditional bias is nondecreasing as prior strength eta increases in the fixed model.
mbjg25_theorem3_1_squared_bias_monotonic.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1015, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A Equations 6-7 and 12-13; source.txt:443-450 and 1497-1517 and 1606-1637

mbjg25_theorem3_2_squared_bias_convexity.statement: Theorem 3.2 states that squared bias is convex as a function of true product quality.
mbjg25_theorem3_2_squared_bias_convexity.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1015, Theorem 3.2 and Appendix A Equation 18; source.txt:460-469 and 1664-1674

mbjg25_theorem3_2_squared_bias_minimizer.statement: Theorem 3.2 states that squared bias has a global minimum at the prior mean alpha_tilde/(alpha_tilde+beta_tilde).
mbjg25_theorem3_2_squared_bias_minimizer.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1015, Theorem 3.2 and Appendix A; source.txt:460-469 and 1655-1663

mbjg25_theorem3_2_variance_concavity.statement: Theorem 3.2 states that posterior-rating variance is concave as a function of true product quality.
mbjg25_theorem3_2_variance_concavity.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1015, Theorem 3.2 and Appendix A Equation 11; source.txt:460-469 and 1533-1561

mbjg25_theorem3_2_variance_maximizer.statement: Theorem 3.2 states that posterior-rating variance has a global maximum at true quality one half.
mbjg25_theorem3_2_variance_maximizer.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1015, Theorem 3.2 and Appendix A Equation 11; source.txt:460-469 and 1533-1561

mbjg25_theorem3_1_endpoint_zero_evidence.statement: At q_v=0, the variance numerator t*q_v*(1-q_v) is zero for every prior strength, refuting the printed closed-interval strict wording at the lower endpoint.
mbjg25_theorem3_1_endpoint_zero_evidence.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1015, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A Equation 11; source.txt:443-450 and 1533-1552
mbjg25_theorem3_1_endpoint_zero_evidence.source_note: Checked mathematical evidence for the schema-2 source correction, not a separately advertised paper theorem.

mbjg25_theorem3_1_endpoint_one_evidence.statement: At q_v=1, the variance numerator t*q_v*(1-q_v) is zero for every prior strength, refuting the printed closed-interval strict wording at the upper endpoint.
mbjg25_theorem3_1_endpoint_one_evidence.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1015, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A Equation 11; source.txt:443-450 and 1533-1552
mbjg25_theorem3_1_endpoint_one_evidence.source_note: Checked mathematical evidence for the schema-2 source correction, not a separately advertised paper theorem.

mbjg25_selection_rate.statement: Section 2.3 defines a product's selection rate as its number of selections (equivalently ratings) divided by its lifespan.

mbjg25_individual_producer_unfairness.statement: Equation 5 defines quality-conditional individual producer unfairness as the standard deviation of selection rates among products with the same true quality.
mbjg25_individual_producer_unfairness.source_note: The source denotes the statistic by sigma-hat without spelling out its finite-sample divisor; Lean records the empirical-distribution divisor |U| and the empty-class convention explicitly.

mbjg25_marketplace_producer_unfairness.statement: Marketplace-level producer unfairness is the expectation of quality-conditional individual unfairness over true product qualities.
mbjg25_marketplace_producer_unfairness.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), p. 1014, paragraph after Equation 5; source.txt:386-390

mbjg25_thompson_sampling_choice.statement: In each responsive-market period, Thompson sampling draws one posterior-quality value for every currently available product and chooses a product attaining the maximum draw.
mbjg25_thompson_sampling_choice.source_note: Lean exposes the exact draw-a-joint-profile then argmax policy map; the source's independent Beta posteriors instantiate the supplied joint belief law, while calibrated simulation code is empirical implementation scope.

mbjg25_eq4_expected_regret.statement: Equation 4 defines finite-horizon expected regret as the expected sum of the quality gap between the best currently available product and the selected product.

mbjg25_appendix_c_responsive_mse_decompo.statement: Appendix C Equations 19-20 apply the tower law over random review count and decompose responsive-market conditional MSE into expected squared fixed-model bias plus expected fixed-model variance.

mbjg25_positive_prior_shape.statement: The fixed prior shape has positive total mass so its Beta mean and scaled prior parameters are defined.
mbjg25_positive_prior_shape.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Section 2.1 and Theorems 3.1-3.2; source.txt:233-276 and 443-469

mbjg25_positive_fixed_time.statement: The fixed-setting results evaluate quality after a positive number of elapsed review timesteps.
mbjg25_positive_fixed_time.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Sections 2.2-3.1 and Appendix A; source.txt:288-292 and 443-469 and 1497-1552

mbjg25_nonnegative_review_count.statement: Elapsed time and review-count mass are nonnegative in the fixed and responsive models.
mbjg25_nonnegative_review_count.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Sections 2.1-2.2 and Appendix A; source.txt:203-292 and 1533-1552

mbjg25_quality_lower_bound.statement: Every product's Bernoulli true quality satisfies 0 <= q_v.

mbjg25_quality_upper_bound.statement: Every product's Bernoulli true quality satisfies q_v <= 1.

mbjg25_corrected_interior_quality_lower_.statement: The corrected strict-variance conclusion restricts true quality to 0 < q_v so that the Bernoulli variance numerator is positive.
mbjg25_corrected_interior_quality_lower_.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A Equation 11; source.txt:443-450 and 1533-1552 and 1638-1650
mbjg25_corrected_interior_quality_lower_.source_note: Formalized source-correction condition implied by the source formula.

mbjg25_corrected_interior_quality_upper_.statement: The corrected strict-variance conclusion restricts true quality to q_v < 1 so that the Bernoulli variance numerator is positive.
mbjg25_corrected_interior_quality_upper_.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A Equation 11; source.txt:443-450 and 1533-1552 and 1638-1650
mbjg25_corrected_interior_quality_upper_.source_note: Formalized source-correction condition implied by the source formula.

mbjg25_nonnegative_prior_strength.statement: Prior strength eta is nonnegative in the source parameterization (alpha_hat,beta_hat)=(eta*alpha_tilde,eta*beta_tilde).
mbjg25_nonnegative_prior_strength.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Section 2.1 and Theorem 3.1; source.txt:270-276 and 443-450

mbjg25_weak_prior_strength_order.statement: The nondecreasing/nonincreasing clauses compare a lower prior strength eta_low with eta_high satisfying eta_low <= eta_high.
mbjg25_weak_prior_strength_order.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A; source.txt:443-450 and 1606-1650

mbjg25_strict_prior_strength_order.statement: Strict variance decrease compares prior strengths satisfying eta_low < eta_high.
mbjg25_strict_prior_strength_order.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A; source.txt:443-450 and 1638-1650

mbjg25_eq20_positive_rating_count.statement: Equation 20's observed-rating weighted-average expression is evaluated for a positive observed rating count n.

mbjg25_eq20_bayesian_rating_equivalence.statement: Equation 20 simplifies the convex combination of the observed positive-rating share and population baseline C to (k+m*C)/(n+m), which is the binary posterior formula with pseudo-counts m*C and m*(1-C).
mbjg25_eq20_bayesian_rating_equivalence.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Appendix D, Equation 20 and following paragraph; source.txt:1810-1835
mbjg25_eq20_bayesian_rating_equivalence.source_note: The printed Beta(C,1) label is corrected to Beta(C,1-C), the unique shape whose mean is C and whose strength-one scaling yields Equation 20.

mbjg25_eq21_corrected_ordinal_posterior_.statement: Corrected Equation 21: under a Dirichlet prior, ordinal posterior expected rating is the rating-value-weighted sum of prior pseudo-count plus observed count, divided by total prior plus observed mass.
mbjg25_eq21_corrected_ordinal_posterior_.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Appendix E, Equation 21 and surrounding Dirichlet-prior paragraphs; source.txt:1903-2029
mbjg25_eq21_corrected_ordinal_posterior_.source_note: The printed display omits alphaHat from both sums; the notation and adjacent paragraphs uniquely require the prior pseudo-count terms.

mbjg25_eq21_printed_zero_prior_compariso.statement: The expression printed in Equation 21 is exactly the zero-prior special case of the corrected Dirichlet posterior expected-rating formula.
mbjg25_eq21_printed_zero_prior_compariso.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Appendix E, Equation 21 and following prior-strength paragraph; source.txt:1903-2029
mbjg25_eq21_printed_zero_prior_compariso.source_note: Checked comparison evidence for the formalized Equation 21 source correction.

mbjg25_appendix_f_k_sampling_rule.statement: Appendix F defines k-sampling by taking the k products with the highest values in the sampled reward profile and selecting uniformly from that top-k set.
mbjg25_appendix_f_k_sampling_rule.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Appendix F, k-sampling definition; source.txt:2090-2175

mbjg25_appendix_f_k_one_endpoint.statement: At k=1, k-sampling selects the profile argmax and is the one-profile choice step of traditional Thompson sampling.
mbjg25_appendix_f_k_one_endpoint.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Appendix F, paragraph after k-sampling definition; source.txt:2090-2175

mbjg25_appendix_f_market_size_endpoint.statement: When k equals the number of products in the market, k-sampling is uniform random selection over the whole market.
mbjg25_appendix_f_market_size_endpoint.source_location: ICWSM 19(1), Appendix F, paragraph after k-sampling definition; source.txt:2090-2175
